newsitem.title: FRANCE: Turnout up in French parliamentary election.
newsitem.headline: Turnout up in French parliamentary election.

text.p: Voter turnout in Sunday's runoff round of France's parliamentary election stood at 24.08 percent at midday (1000 GMT), against 17.47 percent at the same time in the 1993 election, the Interior Ministry said.
Among key factors in the election is the behaviour of the high proportion of electors -- 31.55 percent -- who stayed away from the polls in the first round a week ago.
The outcome of the election was thrown wide open after the Socialist-Communist bloc scored an upset win against the ruling centre-right coalition in the first round.

Polling stations opened at 8 a.m. (0600 GMT) in mainland France and are due to close at 8 p.m. (1800 GMT), when the first results projections will be released. The weather was sunny in most parts but rain was forecast in the south.
In the first round, when the combined left polled 40.1 percent of the vote to 36.5 for the centre-right, candidates were separated by less than two percentage points in 80 of the 577 constituencies.
